turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“I’ve been feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially toward the end of the day—it’s gotten to the point that it’s hard to take care of myself. I also have some mild double vision. I’ve been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and had multiple illnesses in the recent past.”
Does your weakness and double vision noticeably improve after resting, or does it remain constant regardless of rest?

“It definitely improves after I rest, but it doesn’t fully go away, and when I’m up and active again toward the end of the day it comes back worse. The double vision also gets better when I’ve been resting.”
Have you noticed any drooping of your eyelids (ptosis), particularly as the day progresses or after prolonged use?

“Now that you ask, yes—my eyelids seem to droop more as the day goes on, and it’s worse after I’ve been using my eyes or staying active. When I rest, both the drooping and the double vision get noticeably better.”
Have you noticed any difficulty with chewing, swallowing, or speaking, particularly after eating a full meal or talking for an extended period?

“I have noticed some mild trouble chewing and swallowing when I’ve been talking a lot or eating a full meal, and it feels worse later in the day; speaking for long stretches also seems to tire me out.”
[DDX] Myasthenia gravis, Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome, Botulism, Brainstem lesion (e.g., stroke, demyelinating disease), Tick-borne illness (e.g., Lyme disease)
